items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the round-feedback form after the sprint-47 live clicks); filed by Claude
items.title: Roads are a tree plus a detour test, and only villages above a size spur: no lattice, and round 6's tail inside 35 s
items.design:
MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 50. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the density form): the village spur floor is 40,000 heads (the ladder's ~p90; median road pass 18 s loaded, 1 of 16 seeds under 10 s), size read as the population step's headcount; a border link ends ONLY on a town or a spurring village (LOGISTICS.md § 4). The street carpet is not this item's: BL-1130 (centres consolidate) thins the centres upstream, and this item's "no lattice on the densest seed" is read after it.

ROUND 2 (the lane's own findings and the settle review): fix the floor at 40,000 as the constant; border endpoints restricted to towns and spurring villages; road_generation.cpp's two hand-written cache clears (~616-619, ~689-691) replaced by invalidate_logistics_caches so the new nearest-anchor field is never missed; the loading bar's roads weight (hard_coded_world.cpp ~495, 38,000 ms) and kBorderUnitsPerNation re-measured; road_generation_harness's "R2 highway tier reachable when qualified" FAILS on 0 of 8 seeds, identically on b03fd52e -- find why (the percentile gate, the two-major-endpoints rule, or the harness's qualified regen) and fix the cause or split it to its own item with the reading; never weaken the row.

SPRINT 48 CUT (Ben, 2026-09-25, the cut form): BL-1077 (village roads cost) is FOLDED IN. Its target joins this done-when: generate_roads under ~10 s Release on the library seeds, read after the spur floor; if the floor alone does not reach it, BL-1077's bound (one multi-source search per centre, or a shared reach field, digest-neutral by itself) is this item's second step. THE 35 s IS JUDGED ON THE WHOLE TAIL, jointly with BL-1117 (settle tick one), which joins the sprint with its fix: on seed 0 the settle is ~56 s Release, tick 1 alone 38.5 s, so roads alone cannot meet it.

FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben, walking round 6: "we also need many fewer roads... it should be heavily discouraged to build a lattice of roads"; he chose the tree plus a detour test over "no second path", and spurs only for villages above a size). LOGISTICS.md § 4 carries the rule; STARTUP.md § Round 6 carries the 35 s target.

THE WORK. (1) Replace the relative-neighbour redundancy edges with the DETOUR TEST: after the Kruskal MST, a candidate link between two centres is laid only when the network's route between them costs more than 2x the direct A* route (one constant, named). The percentile rationing of loops applies to the loops the test admits (a delegated reading that keeps BL-618/BL-621 intact; Ben may overturn). (2) A village lays a spur only above a size floor, MEASURED on the 16 curated seeds first (Rule 0b: road tiles, spur count and pass time per floor candidate). (3) The border link rule is unchanged.

A WORLD-MOVER: every road digest and the sweep pins move -- read road tile counts, pass time (gen_step_costs --finish) and the haulage baseline (memory: goldens cannot see trade) on the 16 seeds before and after, then ONE re-bless.

DONE WHEN. No lattice on a capture of the densest seed; road pass time and tile count recorded old -> new per seed; round 6's tail lands within 35 s of arrival on seeds 0 and 28 in Release (gen_step_costs); one re-bless; road_generation_harness green (connectivity held). CARRIED to sprint 49 at the sprint 48 close (2026-10-04): owed R4 a quiet Release gen_step_costs run on 16 seeds (road tiles and pass time per seed, old -> new, against ~10 s); R6 an isolated haulage reading of this change (or fold into BL-1165); R7 a cold review of round 4 (8b921ee6, directed paths).

items.title: A built processor gets its inputs: 85% running and at most 5% input-starved at handoff
items.design: TARGETS RAISED (Ben, 2026-10-08): G1 >= 85% running at handoff, plus G1b <= 5% input-starved (now, or decommissioned after starving), 16 seeds. 70% had no recorded reason beyond a first stretch from a 17.6% baseline; G1 alone counts a plant idled for want of a buyer as failure, so starvation gets its own target. CARRIED from sprint 49 (Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07: close with G1 unmet, carry it to sprint 50 as a logistics item). The 16-seed market_viability reading on main after BL-1183 C1: G1 54.7% of built processors running at handoff against Ben's 70% (G2 54.4 and G3 88.9 pass). About a quarter of built processors are already decommissioned by the handoff, and by their last reported state almost all were input-starved (half A: 578 of 674). Diagnose which inputs fail to arrive, at which markets, and why - no producer within reach, a producer whose surplus is not dispatched, or a dispatch the margin refuses - then fix the cause in the network or dispatch, not by clamping the loss reflex. Re-measure construction stalls here too: whether a stalled site is ever abandoned (BL-1183 C3) is still unruled. Judge it on the market-viability skill, 16 seeds.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50, deferred by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: Long-term viability: plants running at handoff are still running at play tick 50
items.design: DEFERRED from sprint 50 (Ben, 2026-10-09: 'push the long term viability work for another sprint, after the various other gameplay loops are settled'). Target carried: G1 at tick 50 >= 85% (market-viability; reported, not gated, in sprint 50). FOUND (starve_trace_probe, f98d43df, shipped code before sprint 50's wave 2b): of 665 plants lost handoff->t50, 386 starved. (1) STEEL: a background-firm CONSTRUCTION BOOM - on 33 starving markets 725 sites draw steel at t50, 701 background-owned (ports/hubs 264, food 181, fuel 79); site need ~373/tick vs processors ~35; making builds read steel scarcity is a NEW AI GRANT (raise it). (2) UNDELIVERED HAULS: copper ore - dispatcher 'would send' in 36/47 cases, arrivals ~8/tick; split Logistic Points cap / one-destination-per-pass / goods sent elsewhere (SUPPLY/LOGISTICS). (3) POOL-HELD STOCK: 42 plants starve while stock sits unlisted in other pools at the market; split processor reservation vs sell-order floor (MARKETS). (4) FUEL->PROPELLANT COLD START: with generation bounded by want, neither chain stands at generation and no launchpad exists on any seed; space access depends on settle/play building both (PRODUCTION, ERAS gate). Ruled healthy, keep: fair-price ceiling (cf off: -8.0 G1t50), background pull (cf off: -1.4), households' first draw. Re-measure with the probe after sprint 50 merges before designing.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50 PROPELLANT cold review; backlogged by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: A rival's launch fuel is not drained by its own scorer or the space programme - or it is, by ruling
items.design: BACKLOGGED by Ben (2026-10-09, launch fuel form) - both questions open, for a ruling when space access matters. Context: MARKETS.md step 4 reserves a pad pool's propellant from auto-surplus (Ben 2026-10-09; may still be sold by a standing order). Cold review of the PROPELLANT lane found three rival paths that ignore that reservation: (a) corp_ai.cpp listable_surplus (~2572) uses processor_reservation, so the trade candidate places an uncapped sell order that empties the pad pool, re-placed each time stock rebuilds; (b) the scorer's directed dispatch (~2735) has no reservation and can haul pad propellant to the capital market on the same body; (c) space_programme.cpp (~140-175) buys 50-unit lumps from the pool holding most unreserved stock - pad pools are now where propellant piles up. Q1: should the scorer sell/haul only above the pad reservation? Q2: should the space programme buy only the excess? No seed had a launchpad at t50 in sprint 50, so the effect is latent.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: Hit the total and major nation targets every time, by a lean and then in-world reconciliation
items.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10, option C; always hit): NATION_GENERATION.md § The nation count is a target. Total <= 40, major 1..6, total >= major. Stage 1, the lean: the total sets placement seed density; the major target leans charter-capital concentration. Stage 2, reconciliation by history verbs: conquest/absorption (too many nations), a subject freed or a province seceding (too few), a national champion chartered in the richest championless minor (too few majors), a cross-border buy-out (too many majors). OPEN before build: which span runs reconciliation; how the richest minor is read; buy-out pricing; how the merge pass's min-territory stop composes with a target. MEASURE FIRST: the natural total and major counts across the 16 library seeds (living polities run ~40-115, so the 40 cap reconciles on nearly every seed). Gate: every library seed lands on both targets across a grid of target pairs, each correction recorded as a history event.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: A setup round before Life, carrying the total and major nation targets
items.design: RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10): STARTUP.md § Rounds, A SETUP ROUND PRECEDES LIFE. It takes the two nation targets before the Life round builds the world. OPEN: what else it holds (Ben: 'along with the existing choices at each phase' - whether per-round leans move here or stay on their rounds), and where it sits against System. The next design step of sprint 53.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: Retire the wizard globe; the Life round draws the homeworld on the pass rounds' 2D map
items.design: DESIGNED (Ben, 2026-10-10): STARTUP.md § The Life map. The globe (48-slice render) is retired; System keeps its system drawing; the Life round draws the Life-gate world on the 2D map the pass rounds use, which holds through the Culture wait. Retire the globe code and its captures; update any golden or verify script that names it. OPEN: whether the Life map may pan/zoom for reading (no steering input either way). Needs a live click.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: The seat becomes a nation selection screen: majors only, a six-part nation card, take_seat names a major
items.design: DESIGNED (Ben, 2026-10-10): STARTUP.md § The seat. Rows are the majors (count = major target). Card (seven parts; the seventh, history, is BL-1295): territory highlighted on the map, population and GDP, treasury/debt/budget weights, the champion (today's firm card), resource profile and deposits, neighbours with stances and grudges. take_seat names a major and seats its champion; its ACTIONS.json entry and the question_log surface question ('which nation am I?') change with it. Shaped for up to six humans, one major each; the prototype seats one (NR-1025). Needs a live click.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: Minor nations run shallow: treasury, budget weights and tariffs on a slow cadence, no law, no specialist
items.design: DESIGNED (Ben, 2026-10-10): NATIONS.md § Major and minor nations. A minor keeps treasury, budget weights, tariffs and garrisons; is re-scored on a slower cadence than a major; enacts no law beyond what generation left it; hosts no specialist (background firms stay - NR-1027). Determinism: the cadence keys on the ascending-id set, like the major stagger.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: The specialist roster is the set of champions: exactly one per major nation
items.design: DESIGNED (Ben, 2026-10-10): CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 1, AMENDED FORWARD 2026-10-10. One specialist per major, chartered in its richest affording centre; none in a minor; other affording centres spend on background firms. Overturns the fixed count of 8 and the 2026-09-17 multi-seat nation rule. Gate: market-viability and the 16-seed sweep - fewer specialists moves the economy, so it waits on the shelf/trade landing and takes a re-bless with Ben's go.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: The player governs its nation: budget, tariff and law verbs, the nation step skips it, and the nation musters
items.design: DESIGNED IN PART (Ben, 2026-10-10): NATIONS.md § What a nation does each tick (the player's nation is never scored; moves 2-4 run on the player's weights); MILITARY.md § The muster interface (the nation raises units and buys their equipment as a real buyer on the order book, NR-1028); CONCEPT.md § Territorial existence (eliminated at no territory). OPEN: the verb set and its seam validation (untrusted-input rule), who builds and owns a military base, the elimination check. Every new control gets an ACTIONS.json entry.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
items.title: Detectors for the five history patterns, measured across the 16 library seeds before any target is built
items.design: DESIGNED (Ben, 2026-10-10): GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § History patterns. One predicate per pattern over the history record (lapse_event + span records), naming the polities it touched; emits pattern tags carried polity -> nation (NATION_GENERATION's fold). FIRST: measure how often each pattern already happens across the 16 library seeds, unforced - it sets each lean's size and whether reconciliation has much to do. The detectors are also the gates of BL-1287, BL-1288, BL-1289.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
items.title: The rise and fall: one realm grows largest through successive victories early in Empires and breaks down within a window, every world
items.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10): CIVILISATION.md § How an empire actually falls (THE RISE AND FALL IS TARGETED). Overturns 'never scheduled' for one realm's window only; the fall is still breakdown + secession. OPEN: the window's span and how 'early' is read; lean then reconciliation verbs; the non-hegemony cap (NR-1034).

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
items.title: The late culture: one distant culture develops slower from its isolation and is colonised in Exploration, every world
items.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10): EXPLORATION.md § A colony is a subject (THE LATE CULTURE IS TARGETED). A development lag read from remoteness, carried from the Culture round; bound by the ordinary subjection verbs. OPEN: the lag mechanism (no development-lag mechanism exists today), which culture is chosen (NR-1034), reconciliation if the lean misses.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
items.title: A world war in every world: population, industry, roads and ports, and treasuries lost, and the world redevelops before 1960
items.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10): INDUSTRIALISATION.md § A world war in every world. Overturns 'permitted, never forced'. Builds on the PROPOSED mutual-defence spread (the clause exists in code; no world-war, conscript or refugee code exists). OPEN: razing industry and capital is not designed; war debt; redevelopment pace so 1960 opens on a recovery; Alarm interplay. Moves the 1960 economy: re-bless with Ben's go.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
items.title: Civil war as a lean: a splitting realm's halves fight; soldiers die, and a famine and displacement mechanism takes civilians
items.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10): CIVILISATION.md and MILITARY_HISTORY.md § Armies are distinct from population. Secession gains a fighting step; civilian deaths only via a separately authored famine/displacement mechanism (the door the 2026-09-09 ruling left open). OPEN: the mechanism itself; guard against the empty-region failure.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
items.title: Revolution as a lean in Industrialisation: post-Exploration disparity between a nation's cities breeds a splinter that can take the whole nation
items.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10): INDUSTRIALISATION.md § Revolution. Off the post-Exploration city disparity (inequality stays between nations and cities, never households). Overturns 'no regime reset' for this span. OPEN: the splinter verb, what a takeover changes (regime field, name, polity id), its tag.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the history-patterns form); filed by Claude
items.title: The nation card's history: pattern tags, a short key-event timeline, and a link to the History ledger filtered to the nation
items.design: DESIGNED (Ben, 2026-10-10): STARTUP.md § The seat, the card's seventh item. Reads BL-1286's tags and the lapse events of the polities that folded into the nation. Needs a live click.
